items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: if it doesn’t come out of Louis Armstrong, it doesn’t swing

ctx.x: Even in the jazz education thing. Hmm. Well now we enter the realm of conjecture. How do I know? Am I copping a plea? I don’t know. I mean, like I say, I can conjecture. I mean I think the bottom line is simply somebody is going to teach what they feel most comfortable with and what they most like. So the generation of educators that are out there in the jazz college scene or jazz high school, whatever, those are the guys, they really, I mean maybe they listen to Duke, maybe they listen to Bix and the older guys…

a lot of other things. So whatever is going to get taught is going to get taught, it’s going to reflect the guys who are teaching it. And if that’s what they’re into, that’s what’s going to be the focus.
